title: ProofFlow
subtitle: Checked repairs before the next batch

slides.title: ProofFlow
slides.notes: ProofFlow targets operations engineers maintaining small merchant revenue imports. It proposes code repairs, runs them on a designated isolated worker, independently checks source occurrences, and requires exact-version approval before a fresh batch. This is a private synthetic demonstration, not a public production service. Sources: docs/product.md; docs/contract.md; docs/evidence/phase6-scheduled-portable-demo-2026-11-08.json.

slides.title: A successful run can assign the wrong owner

slides.title: The repair workflow
slides.notes: The operator supplies source/data and approves the exact declarative contract. The dispatcher requests bounded proposals through Vultr Serverless Inference; candidate code is untrusted. Every execution is on the designated worker. Source-derived deterministic checks and protected canaries decide whether a candidate may be reviewed. AWAITING_APPROVAL is not activation. Exact-version approval permits another isolated execution on genuinely new input bytes. Product PR actions remain separate. Sources: docs/product.md; docs/contract.md; orchestrator/repair_dispatcher.py; docs/evidence/phase3-acceptance-2026-11-04.json; docs/evidence/phase4-acceptance-2026-11-05.json.

slides.title: Vultr deployment and trust boundaries
slides.notes: Two existing Vultr Compute VMs separate control and untrusted execution. The control VM runs the private web API, trusted dispatcher, PostgreSQL durable state/budget and restricted independent verifier. The worker uses gVisor runsc/systrap under systemd cgroups, authenticated mTLS and durable cleanup receipts. Only the trusted dispatcher receives provider and dedicated GitHub App credentials; candidate and verifier do not. No candidate execution on control or development hosts. Architecture reflects the implemented runtime, not older Next.js planning. Sources: docs/architecture.md; docs/sandbox.md; docs/evidence/phase5-binary-acceptance-2026-11-07.json. Event alignment: https://lablab.build/ai-hackathons/vultr-hackathon (checked Nov8 KST).

slides.title: One recorded repair, then a fresh batch
slides.notes: The real November8 run made one Vultr qwen3.8-flash-next request, changed source, passed candidate/ownership-canary/quarantine-canary comparisons with confirmed cleanup, downloaded the evidence ZIP, received an automated synthetic exact-version test approval and completed a different batch. Reservation $0.027853 is not an invoice. These counts describe this run, not benchmark performance. The139.04s edited video preserves raw clips and a cut/hold manifest. A completed-batch receipt card is explicitly a summary, because the raw browser moved on before a readable completion frame. Two later demo harness errors remain failed and reconciled. Source: docs/evidence/phase6-scheduled-portable-demo-2026-11-08.json; docs/demo.md.

slides.title: A deliberate infinite loop is contained
slides.notes: This is the separately labeled real zero-inference loop segment, not AI output. Worker readback confirms signal9, no collected output, cleanup confirmed and kernel writers absent. Missing output correctly produces FAILED_INFRA; no verifier acceptance is fabricated. The browser harness initially assumed report.worker on an infrastructure failure; public report is null. Its failed receipt is preserved and reconciled against the committed worker journal. Resource limits are1CPU,768MiB memory,0swap; network denial and other limits were tested in prior actual containment probes. No claim of universal containment or formal security proof. Sources: docs/evidence/phase6-scheduled-portable-demo-2026-11-08.json; docs/evidence/phase5-binary-acceptance-2026-11-07.json.

slides.title: The synthetic comparison
slides.notes: Frozen96-job comparison:24 cases x4 approaches,18 repairable plus6 ambiguous per approach. A uses the full API workflow; B accepts successful collected execution then grades independently; C removes witness rows from repair feedback; D is a fixed deterministic rebuild. A and C equal repair coverage; D performs best in this narrow contract and reuses the positive template. This does not establish AI superiority. One repeat, shared fault families/templates, no independent human oracle review; one preserved A harness interruption remains in the denominator. Sources: eval/final-comparison-2026-11-06.md; eval/final-comparison-2026-11-06.json. The artifact checker was rerun offline; no source executed or model called for this package.

slides.title: What this prototype supports
slides.notes: Target users and business value are hypotheses, not measured customer traction or ROI. Supported scope:one<=16KiB Python file, pinned pandas, small UTF-8 transaction/customer CSVs, approved synthetic merchant-revenue contract. Every occurrence must be accounted for; conflicts and missing declared attributes hold the batch. Public access, MIT ownership clearance and submission remain unapproved; the repository stays private. Offline key custody is explicitly deferred by the owner; lost trusted deletion authority and compromised-host recovery remain gaps. Project owner is the only confirmed human contributor; Codex assists development. No independent human security sign-off. Sources: docs/product.md; docs/contract.md; docs/risks.md; docs/release.md.
